- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) mid-horizon, adjust forecast downward by 3–5% per day to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend + negative sentiment, expect mean reversion; cap forecast decline at 2–3% per day.  
- If forecast spikes >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.5) and price is volatile, forecast should be closer to 10-day moving average, not 30-day.  
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ days, reduce next forecast by 2–4% to avoid lagged overreaction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is positive but price is falling, assume sentiment is overvalued; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days.
